value.lexeme:
>-
      Something that happens at a point or over an interval.
      Aligned with BFO:Occurrent / PROV:Activity. Instantaneous
      events use occurred_at. Processes with duration use
      started_at / ended_at (Allen's interval algebra).

value.lexeme:

      Anything with a stable, globally unique identity.
      Aligned with BFO Independent Continuant: exists on its own,
      bears qualities, participates in processes.

value.lexeme:
>-
      A typed, directed edge between two entities.
      Reified as a class so relations can carry metadata
      (strength, confidence, temporal validity).

value.lexeme:
>-
      A continuously derived quality that emerges from patterns
      of Events between Entities. Aligned with BFO:Specifically
      Dependent Continuant (Quality) and SSN/SOSA:Observation.
      A Signal inheres in its bearer(s) — it does not exist
      independently. It is computed, not asserted: derived on
      demand from the Event log and Entity graph via a named
      algorithm. Domain projects define signal types, algorithms,
      and interpretation semantics. The Signal class captures
      the universal pattern: something measurable that emerges
      from activity, has a current value, and is recomputable
      from the underlying data.
value.value: A continuously derived quality that emerges from patterns of Events between Entities. Aligned with BFO:Specifically Dependent Continuant (Quality) and SSN/SOSA:Observation. A Signal inheres in its bearer(s) — it does not exist independently. It is computed, not asserted: derived on demand from the Event log and Entity graph via a named algorithm. Domain projects define signal types, algorithms, and interpretation semantics. The Signal class captures the universal pattern: something measurable that emerges from activity, has a current value, and is recomputable from the underlying data.

invention_search.lexeme:
>-
        No vocabulary among QUDT, UCUM, ISO 80000 and the VIM cited above
        names how a source qualifies the number it states. The QUDT schema
        carries standardUncertainty and relativeStandardUncertainty, which
        quantify a measurement's dispersion rather than a source's hedge, and
        minInclusive and maxInclusive, which constrain a datatype rather than
        describe a stated bound. VIM 4.6 defines nominal quantity value as a
        rounded or approximate value characterizing a measuring instrument,
        not a reported measurement, and VIM defines no term for an
        open-ended statement. UCUM codes units and discards annotations by
        definition. ISO 80000-2 supplies the relation sign read as is
        approximately equal to, a mathematical symbol rather than a
        qualification of a reported value. The enum name and its five values
        are therefore local.
invention_search.value: No vocabulary among QUDT, UCUM, ISO 80000 and the VIM cited above names how a source qualifies the number it states. The QUDT schema carries standardUncertainty and relativeStandardUncertainty, which quantify a measurement's dispersion rather than a source's hedge, and minInclusive and maxInclusive, which constrain a datatype rather than describe a stated bound. VIM 4.6 defines nominal quantity value as a rounded or approximate value characterizing a measuring instrument, not a reported measurement, and VIM defines no term for an open-ended statement. UCUM codes units and discards annotations by definition. ISO 80000-2 supplies the relation sign read as is approximately equal to, a mathematical symbol rather than a qualification of a reported value. The enum name and its five values are therefore local.

value.lexeme:
>-
      Controlled classification of a reported quantity. Every value except
      OTHER is a name minted in the QUDT quantity-kind vocabulary, spelled as
      QUDT spells it. OTHER is local and records that no listed kind fits. The
      list is deliberately short and grows by adding values, never by
      redefining one.
value.value: Controlled classification of a reported quantity. Every value except OTHER is a name minted in the QUDT quantity-kind vocabulary, spelled as QUDT spells it. OTHER is local and records that no listed kind fits. The list is deliberately short and grows by adding values, never by redefining one.

value.lexeme:
>-
      How the source qualifies the number it states. It records the form of
      the statement and never the number: value_lower, value_upper and unit
      stay exactly as the source gives them. Leaving it unset is the honest
      value when the source's form is unclear. The list is deliberately short
      and grows by adding values, never by redefining one.
value.value: How the source qualifies the number it states. It records the form of the statement and never the number: value_lower, value_upper and unit stay exactly as the source gives them. Leaving it unset is the honest value when the source's form is unclear. The list is deliberately short and grows by adding values, never by redefining one.

value.lexeme:

          stated number unchanged; the approximation is recorded here and is
          never converted into an invented interval.

value.lexeme:

          number and value_upper stays absent, because the source states no
          upper bound and inventing one would report something it does not
          say.

value.lexeme:

value.lexeme:
>-
      An individually identified seismic event (as opposed to an aggregately
      counted earthquake population), such as the named 2016 Mw 7.1 Romanche
      transform-fault earthquake and its named subevents. Magnitude is carried
      through the Quantified mixin (quantity_kind e.g. "moment magnitude");
      domain-time of unstated precision is carried through the TemporalExtent
      mixin's temporal_precision rather than invented into occurred_at.
value.value: An individually identified seismic event (as opposed to an aggregately counted earthquake population), such as the named 2016 Mw 7.1 Romanche transform-fault earthquake and its named subevents. Magnitude is carried through the Quantified mixin (quantity_kind e.g. "moment magnitude"); domain-time of unstated precision is carried through the TemporalExtent mixin's temporal_precision rather than invented into occurred_at.

search.lexeme:
>-
            Checked, from memory, the OGC/CGI GeoSciML structural-geology
            vocabulary and general earth-science term lists for a controlled
            class covering named ridge segments, ridge-transform
            intersections, oceanic core complexes, and non-transform
            discontinuities as used in mid-ocean-ridge tectonics. No exact
            class names or a verifiable URL could be certified without

invention_search.lexeme:
>-
        The cited SOSA/SSN, VIM, Frascati, SEPIO, and Micropublications
        vocabularies were checked for exact generic Campaign and Instrument
        classes. SOSA/SSN uses Sensor, VIM uses measuring instrument, and no
        exact generic Campaign class was found. The accepted pack keeps the
        shorter local class names and records that choice here. CRediT names
        the fourteen roles and defines each, and ContributorRole follows its
        naming, but it is a term list with no classes, so the mixin
        Contribution and the class ContributionRelation that carry a role in a
        graph are local shapes and are recorded here. The same five
        vocabularies were checked for what a source does with a hypothesis it
        has raised. SEPIO models an assertion's evidence lines and their
        support or refutation, and Micropublications models one statement
        supporting or challenging another; both describe a relation between
        two things, not the source's own disposition of its own hypothesis.
        No term was found for it, so the enum HypothesisDisposition and the
        mixin Evaluative that marks which slots carry such a value are local
        and are recorded here. The same vocabularies were checked for what a
        record's assertion is about. SOSA/SSN defines feature of interest,
        the thing whose property an observation estimates, which fits an
        observation and not a claim, a count or an asserted ratio, and RDF 1.1
        Concepts defines subject as the position a statement is about, for
        every statement and not only a measurement. The pack borrows the RDF
        term, so subject is cited rather than invented and feature of interest
        is recorded here as the narrower term that was considered.

value.lexeme: A bounded research activity such as an observing campaign or study.
value.value: A bounded research activity such as an observing campaign or study.

value.lexeme:
>-
      An attributed statement represented as a graph entity. statement is
      optional and stays empty unless the record's Source declares a licence
      that permits reproducing the sentence; assertion_locator and
      statement_sha256 carry the assertion either way.
value.value: An attributed statement represented as a graph entity. statement is optional and stays empty unless the record's Source declares a licence that permits reproducing the sentence; assertion_locator and statement_sha256 carry the assertion either way.

value.lexeme:
>-
      A record carrying the role in which a source credits a contributor.
      Worn by a relation so the role travels with the credited contribution
      rather than with the person, who may be credited differently elsewhere.
value.value: A record carrying the role in which a source credits a contributor. Worn by a relation so the role travels with the credited contribution rather than with the person, who may be credited differently elsewhere.

value.lexeme:
>-
      A credited contribution from a contributor to a work, campaign, or
      dataset, carrying CONTRIBUTED_TO as its relation_type. contribution_role
      is optional, so a source that credits a person without stating the part
      they played is recorded without inventing one.
value.value: A credited contribution from a contributor to a work, campaign, or dataset, carrying CONTRIBUTED_TO as its relation_type. contribution_role is optional, so a source that credits a person without stating the part they played is recorded without inventing one.

value.lexeme:
>-
      Slots whose value is the source's evaluation of something the source has
      already stated, rather than a further statement of its own. This mixin's
      slot list is the pack's declaration of which slots are evaluative: a
      reader takes it from the compiled contract, and the document-assertion
      adapter refuses an evaluative value that no assertion outside
      HYPOTHESISED formalizes.
value.value: Slots whose value is the source's evaluation of something the source has already stated, rather than a further statement of its own. This mixin's slot list is the pack's declaration of which slots are evaluative: a reader takes it from the compiled contract, and the document-assertion adapter refuses an evaluative value that no assertion outside HYPOTHESISED formalizes.

value.lexeme:
>-
      Source-level modality, optional confidence, the entity the assertion is
      about, and the route and digest that reach the retained assertion behind
      a record. Worn by every claim-bearing record, so the route and the
      subject travel with the claim rather than with a copy of its text.
value.value: Source-level modality, optional confidence, the entity the assertion is about, and the route and digest that reach the retained assertion behind a record. Worn by every claim-bearing record, so the route and the subject travel with the claim rather than with a copy of its text.

value.lexeme:
>-
  Optional reusable vocabulary for attributed claims, observations, methods,
  instruments, investigations, samples, sources, and evidence. Source
  modality remains a domain fact. It is separate from protocol acceptance.
value.value: Optional reusable vocabulary for attributed claims, observations, methods, instruments, investigations, samples, sources, and evidence. Source modality remains a domain fact. It is separate from protocol acceptance.

value.lexeme: Coarse shared modality of what a source asserts.
value.value: Coarse shared modality of what a source asserts.

value.lexeme:
>-
      The role in which a source credits a contributor to a work. Every value
      except OTHER is a role of the CRediT Contributor Roles Taxonomy,
      ANSI/NISO Z39.104-2022, carrying that taxonomy's own definition. OTHER is
      local and records a contribution the taxonomy does not name. A record
      carries the role the source declares, never one inferred from the work.
value.value: The role in which a source credits a contributor to a work. Every value except OTHER is a role of the CRediT Contributor Roles Taxonomy, ANSI/NISO Z39.104-2022, carrying that taxonomy's own definition. OTHER is local and records a contribution the taxonomy does not name. A record carries the role the source declares, never one inferred from the work.

>-

value.lexeme:
>-

value.lexeme:
>-

value.value: Development or design of methodology; creation of models.

value.lexeme:
>-

Programming, software development; designing computer programs; implementation of the computer code and supporting algorithms; testing of existing code components.

value.lexeme:
>-
      What a source does with a hypothesis it has raised. It records the
      source's own disposition, never Malleus's acceptance of it. Unset is the
      honest value when the source raises a hypothesis and never returns to
      it; a disposition these three do not cover is a gap to declare, which is
      how the list grows.
value.value: What a source does with a hypothesis it has raised. It records the source's own disposition, never Malleus's acceptance of it. Unset is the honest value when the source raises a hypothesis and never returns to it; a disposition these three do not cover is a gap to declare, which is how the list grows.

value.lexeme: The source raises the hypothesis and then declines it.
value.value: The source raises the hypothesis and then declines it.

value.lexeme: The source adopts the hypothesis as its own reading.
value.value: The source adopts the hypothesis as its own reading.

value.lexeme:
>-
          The source weighs the hypothesis and leaves it open, stating that
          the evidence does not settle it.
value.value: The source weighs the hypothesis and leaves it open, stating that the evidence does not settle it.

value.value: Generic relation predicates supplied by the research pack.

value.lexeme: Optional confidence stated by the source or adopter.
value.value: Optional confidence stated by the source or adopter.

value.lexeme:
>-
      Opaque route back to the retained assertion this record formalizes: an
      assertion id, a block id, a byte range, a time span in a recording. The
      pack does not interpret it and never assumes the source is a document.
value.value: Opaque route back to the retained assertion this record formalizes: an assertion id, a block id, a byte range, a time span in a recording. The pack does not interpret it and never assumes the source is a document.

value.lexeme: What the source says and how it says it, not whether Malleus accepts it.
value.value: What the source says and how it says it, not whether Malleus accepts it.

value.lexeme:
>-
      Optional CRediT role in which the source credits this contribution. A
      contributor credited under several roles carries one relation per role.
      Unset is the honest value when the source names a contributor without
      stating the part they played.
value.value: Optional CRediT role in which the source credits this contribution. A contributor credited under several roles carries one relation per role. Unset is the honest value when the source names a contributor without stating the part they played.

value.lexeme:
>-
      What the source does with a hypothesis it has raised. It is captured
      from the sentence that disposes of the hypothesis, not from the sentence
      that raises it. Unset for a claim the source never disposes of.
value.value: What the source does with a hypothesis it has raised. It is captured from the sentence that disposes of the hypothesis, not from the sentence that raises it. Unset for a claim the source never disposes of.

value.lexeme:
>-
      Licence the source declares for its own text, as the source declares it.
      Reproducing a source sentence in statement requires one that permits it;
      absent a licence, the sentence stays out of graph state.
value.value: Licence the source declares for its own text, as the source declares it. Reproducing a source sentence in statement requires one that permits it; absent a licence, the sentence stays out of graph state.

value.lexeme: Digest of exact retained source bytes.
value.value: Digest of exact retained source bytes.

value.lexeme:
>-
      Digest of the exact retained assertion text, sha256: followed by 64
      lowercase hexadecimal characters. It compares two records against one
      assertion without the graph carrying the sentence.
value.value: Digest of the exact retained assertion text, sha256: followed by 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters. It compares two records against one assertion without the graph carrying the sentence.

value.lexeme:
>-
      The entity this record's assertion is about, named as a record id that
      resolves in the same change set or the base state. Single and optional:
      a record whose subject the reading does not name leaves it unset, and
      the capture census counts it. The subject is never folded into
      quantity_kind text or into the record's own name, and it is never the
      record itself. The range is Entity, the same declaration a relation's
      endpoints carry, so what an assertion is about stays a reference to a
      thing rather than a sentence about one.
value.value: The entity this record's assertion is about, named as a record id that resolves in the same change set or the base state. Single and optional: a record whose subject the reading does not name leaves it unset, and the capture census counts it. The subject is never folded into quantity_kind text or into the record's own name, and it is never the record itself. The range is Entity, the same declaration a relation's endpoints carry, so what an assertion is about stays a reference to a thing rather than a sentence about one.
